metadata.file_name: 96. Li et al. (2025). Exploring the Evidence to Interpret Differential Item Functioning via Response Process Data.pdf
metadata.title: Exploring the Evidence to Interpret Differential Item Functioning via Response Process Data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the PIAAC 2012 computer-based numeracy assessment for the United States and constructs an analytic dataset at the item level (DIF-free vs gender DIF items) with student-level response process features aggregated/used per item. The authors filter to open-ended items only (31 open-ended items) and exclude 22 items with response missing rates larger than 55%, then further restrict to examinees with process-log records and required background-question responses in the PIAAC U.S. Public Use File 2012. For missingness in the analytic dataset used for DIF detection, they apply MICE with 10 imputations before running the Mantel–Haenszel DIF procedure and then fit supervised ML classifiers (RF and ridge logistic regression) on the resulting DIF labels. The manuscript does not report applying PIAAC complex survey weights (e.g., sampling weights) in the ML modeling; given the ML algorithms used (Random Forest and ridge logistic regression) and the absence of any stated weight variable, the analysis is treated as unweighted, which may limit population-representativeness and standard error calibration under the original multistage sampling design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variable in the ML stage is a DIF label for items (DIF vs DIF-free) derived from Mantel–Haenszel DIF detection, not a PV-based cognitive achievement score. Missing data handling is explicitly reported: the authors use MICE with 10 imputations to replace missingness before DIF detection, so there is no reporting gap for missingness strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PIAAC 2012 computer-based numeracy assessment for the United States (U.S. Public Use File 2012). Restricted to open-ended response item format only (31 open-ended items) and excluded items with response missing rates >55% (22 items excluded) to mitigate missingness effects on DIF detection. Selected examinees who (i) were recorded in the process-data log file and (ii) provided responses to required background questions. After these restrictions, the final dataset contained nine dichotomous numeracy items for DIF labeling and 1,675 examinees (55.40% women, 44.60% men).

main_findings.dataset_used: PIAAC 2012 Numeracy (United States, open-ended items; gender DIF via MH)
main_findings.target_variable: Gender DIF item label (DIF vs DIF-free)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest: Accuracy=0.761, AUC=0.860, Precision=0.621, Recall=0.651, F1=0.636. Ridge logistic regression: Accuracy=0.731, AUC=0.849, Precision=0.554, Recall=0.817, F1=0.660. RF–LR differences: Accuracy +0.030, AUC +0.011, Precision +0.067, Recall −0.166, F1 −0.024.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIAAC 2012 Numeracy (United States, open-ended items) the study leveraged betweenness centrality, initial action timing (FIRST_TIMING), item response time (RT), action-sequence density, and item response scores to predict the gender DIF item label (DIF vs DIF-free), finding that timing features combined with action-sequence features were most informative and that RF and ridge logistic regression achieved comparable overall discrimination (AUC≈0.85–0.86). This indicates that response-process evidence can improve DIF item interpretability beyond DIF statistics alone, supporting test designers in identifying subgroup-specific response strategies (e.g., efficiency/exploration) that may underlie measurement inequities, though the study reports correlational associations rather than causal explanations.

data.outcome_summary: The study proposes a procedure to interpret differential item functioning (DIF) using response process data from the PIAAC 2012 computer-based numeracy assessment in the United States, focusing on gender DIF for open-ended items. After excluding high-missingness items (>55%) and restricting to examinees with process-log and background data, the authors detect gender DIF using Mantel–Haenszel DIF with iterative purification across 10 MICE-imputed datasets, then train supervised classifiers to predict DIF item labels from response-process features and background controls. Random Forest and ridge logistic regression show similar overall performance: RF reaches Accuracy=0.761 and AUC=0.860 (F1=0.636), while ridge logistic regression reaches Accuracy=0.731 and AUC=0.849 (F1=0.660), with RF higher precision and LR higher recall. Across simulated DIF-item percentages (0.14–0.75), accuracy and AUC remain stable, while precision/recall show interactions with DIF prevalence. The authors explicitly frame results as correlational (not causal) and do not report applying PIAAC complex survey weights in the ML stage, which may affect generalizability and uncertainty quantification.
